Class PolicyExpression

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.iam.model.PolicyExpression
public final class PolicyExpression extends Object
A lossless, typed wrapper for the polymorphic oneOf union members used throughout the IAM access-control schemas — the permissions/intersect/subtract entries of an AccessPolicy, PermissionSet and PrincipalPolicy, and the managedPolicies/managedPermissionSets/subtract fields of a PolicyMask.

Each of these union members may be:

  • a bare string — a literal such as "none" / "all", an Equinix Resource Name (ERN), a permissionset:/managedset:/managedpolicy: id, etc.; or
  • a structured value — an inline-permission object, a foreign-access-policy reference, a general permission-set reference, an array of ids, a subtract object, and so on.

Rather than collapsing this to a raw Object (which loses type fidelity and is awkward to inspect), a PolicyExpression preserves whichever form was received on read and emits exactly that form on write. Internally it carries the underlying JsonNode verbatim, so both the string and structured shapes round-trip losslessly; serialization simply re-emits the captured node via toJsonNode() (annotated JsonValue), and deserialization captures any incoming JSON via fromJsonNode(JsonNode) (annotated JsonCreator).

Convenience accessors (isString(), asString(), isArray(), asStringList(), isObject()) let callers branch on the form without depending on Jackson types, while toJsonNode() exposes the full structure for richer navigation.
